children.name: text
children: {b:Appendix 5 - Health and Safety Conditions}
{br}

children.name: text
children: Safety is of paramount importance to Quinn London, as such in addition to all law and regulatory requirements subcontractors should comply with the following health and safety requirements:
{br}

children.name: text
children: {b:{u:Health & Safety Requirements}}
{br}

children.name: text
children: {b:Occupational health} - Health surveillance must be carried out should the task warrant it i.e. Vibration records are to be held in registers if/when operatives are using percussive tools. Blood tests must be offered if the work involves lead to give a before, during and after reading. Dust production must be kept to a minimum by using a means that does not produce dust, using collection bags or damping down. Any fumes created by plant must be exhausted to an outside area. All noisy works are to be carried out at night to protect other personnel.

children.name: text
children: {b:RAMS} - All RAMS must be site/task specific and not generic. All risk assessments must identify all relevant hazards and put in place safety procedures leaving an acceptable level of residual risk.

children.name: text
children: {b:Training} - ALL personnel are required to undergo the T2 Transitions and a Quinn London Construction induction before commencement on site. Names of operatives are required in advance (at least 2 weeks). All operatives attending site must be in possession of a competency card e.g. CSCS (Site operative), CPCS (Plant operator), CISRS (Scaffolder), JIB (Plumber or Electrician), IPAF (Mobile Elevated Works Platform or MEWPs operator), PASMA (Aluminium tower erector), Cat & Genny (Groundworker) or equivalent. Each contractor MUST have a SSSTS certified supervisor and First Aider for site.

children.name: text
children: {b:Temporary Works} - The following items must be covered during any temporary works: The concept of the scheme (designed by a competent engineer), the design brief, the design drawings and specification etc, checking of the design, adequacy of the materials used, site controls of erection, inspection and dismantling, checking of site control, sub-contractor procedures, authority to remove or dismantle.

children.name: text
children: {b:Miscellaneous Plant & Equipment} - All equipment, owned or on hire, must have the relevant, in date inspection certificates. All electrical tools must be 110v and have a Combined Inspection and Test (PAT) test sticker on it dated within the past 3 months. All supervisors are to hold a database of all PAT tested tools on site.

children.name: text
children: {b:Working @ Height} - All contractors are to follow the hierarchy of working @ height. All MEWPs operators are to be IPAF qualified, when operating a Cherry-picker a harness must be worn and a rescue plan must be in place, all tools are to be tied off to prevent them from being dropped. Hop ups (600x600mm) can only be used as a last resort when all other work @ height options have been exhausted i.e. Risers. 300x300mm hop ups are banned from all sites. Scaffolding must be designed by a competent person, inspected every 7 days.

children.name: text
children: {b:Electrical items} - Halogen bulbs are not to be used to prevent the threat of fire; Cable reels can only be used if fully unwound.

children.name: text
children: {b:Lifting} - Lifting equipment may only be used under the control of a Lifting Plan authorised by an Appointed Person. All lifting equipment & lifting accessories must have an in-date inspection certificate. Only CPCS qualified personnel may use the lifting appliances and CPCS qualified slinger/signallers may sling the loads. All lifting personnel must attend the weekly lift team meetings.

children.name: text
children: {b:COSHH} - All COSHH items being used must be supported by a COSHH assessment. If COSHH items are to be stored overnight, they must be contained on a container that can accommodate 110% of the contents. Material Safety Data Sheets (MSDS) must be supplied for 1st Aid and emergency service information purposes.

children.name: text
children: {b:Law} - All works must adhere to the Health & Safety at Work etc. Act 1974, all appropriate regulations, guidance notes and best practice) and QLL H&S policy.

children.name: text
children: {b:Security} - All operatives are to sign in in the QLL signing in book, all stores are to be ordered as per the CLIENT booking in system, and if tools are to be left on site they are to be stored securely in a lock-up container.

children.name: text
children: {b:Logistics} - All deliveries are to be booked in through QLL and adhere to the rules of the Local Authority. All delivery drivers are to wear PPE and are the responsibility of the subcontractor during delivery. All subcontractors are responsible for the unloading, stacking, storing and safe custody of all materials after delivery.

children.name: text
children: {b:RIDDOR} - All accidents, incidents & near misses are to be reported to QLL management team immediately.

children.name: text
children: {b:Inspections} - All weekly inspections must be copied and given to the QLL management team for their records. Examples of these include: - Plant and equipment inspections, scaffolding inspections, lifting accessories, harnesses & lanyards etc.

children.name: text
children: {b:Toolbox Talks} - All TBTs and sign in sheets are to be documented and held on the QLL filing system. (1 TBT per week).

children.name: text
children: {b:PPE} - All operatives are to wear the 5-point PPE (Hard hat to BS EN 397-JSAHB 010-000-200, light eye protection to BS EN 166f, hi-vis vest to EN ISO 20471:2013 class 2, gloves to EN 388:2016+A1:2018 minimum standard 4121 & safety boots to BS EN 20345:2011 class S1P minimum (safety trainers are not to be worn). Shirts with short sleeves as a minimum are to be worn and short trousers are not to be allowed on site.

children.name: text
children: {b:Disciplinary} - Any disciplinary cards issued are to be copied to the QLL management team.

children.name: text
children: {b:Medical information} - The QLL management team must be made aware of any operative who is taking prescription medication and for 1st aid reasons. Any operative who has an allergy (e.g. Penicillin, plasters) or underlying medical condition such as treatment for cancer, respiratory problems or is pregnant etc must bring this to the attention of the QLL management team during inductions.

children.name: text
children: {b:Young persons} - Any contractor employing a young person (under the age of 18 years) must gain the permission of the QLL Construction Director and the Sub-contractor Director and supply QLL management team with a specific RA signed off by the young person's parents/guardians.

children.name: text
children: {b:Housekeeping} - All contractors are responsible for their own housekeeping and keeping the project tidy. Removal from site of all rubbish, excess materials, and packaging in connection with their works, during and on completion.

children.name: text
children: {b:Drug and Alcohol Policy} - The sub-contractor ensures that his employees are aware of and will agree to undertake a drugs and/or alcohol test in any of the following circumstances:

children.name: text
children: a.

children.name: text
children: As part of a random testing programme being carried out by Quinn London or the Client.

children.name: text
children: b.

children.name: text
children: Where, in the opinion of the Quinn London or client team, a sub-contractor's employee may be unfit to work or is demonstrating unusual or uncharacteristic behaviour.

children.name: text
children: Where sub-contractor's employee fails a drugs or alcohol test, refuses to take such a test, or has been caught in possession of, distributing, or selling illicit drugs, the individual will be ejected from the site and a replacement person of equivalent skills and competences will be required.

children.name: text
children: The costs associated with the ejection and any associated delay will be borne by the sub-contractor.

children.name: text
children: Before the commencement of a drugs and/or alcohol test, the Contractor or Sub-contractor ensures that his employees disclose, to the collecting officer, whether they have been on any medication which could be relevant to the test.

children.name: text
children: {b:General Site Rules}

children.name: text
children: a.

children.name: text
children: Correct PPE to be worn at all times (Foot Protection + Hard Hat + Hi Visibility Vest/Jacket). Additional PPE (Gloves/Eye Protection/Dust Mask/Hearing Protection) may also be required depending on the site activity and agreed method statement.

children.name: text
children: b.

children.name: text
children: No machine, item of plant or equipment is to be operated by any person, unless they have been trained and are authorised to do so.

children.name: text
children: c.

children.name: text
children: All machine guarding is to be in place and correctly adjusted, prior to machinery being used.

children.name: text
children: d.

children.name: text
children: Any fault, defect, including damage, or malfunction in any item of machinery, plant, equipment, tool, or guard must be reported immediately.

children.name: text
children: e.

children.name: text
children: No machine, plant or equipment is to be left unattended or cleaned whilst in motion, unless you are authorised to do so.

children.name: text
children: f.

children.name: text
children: No repairs, maintenance or adjustments to machines, plant or equipment are to be carried out, unless you are authorised to do so.

children.name: text
children: g.

children.name: text
children: All substances are only to be used in accordance with the written instructions.

children.name: text
children: h.

children.name: text
children: All substances are to be stored in accordance with the written instructions and are to be returned to the storage after use.

children.name: text
children: i.

children.name: text
children: All hazard notices or warning signs displayed on the premises are to be obeyed.

children.name: text
children: j.

children.name: text
children: All notices displayed in the workplace are to be read and you are to ensure that you understand the instructions.

children.name: text
children: k.

children.name: text
children: All safety equipment and facilities provided are to be used and are not to be misused or wilfully damaged.

children.name: text
children: l.

children.name: text
children: The work area is to be kept clean and tidy at all times.

children.name: text
children: m.

children.name: text
children: All waste is to be disposed of in the correct container.

children.name: text
children: n.

children.name: text
children: All liquid spillages are to be cleaned up immediately.

children.name: text
children: o.

children.name: text
children: All emergency procedures relevant to your work area are to be obeyed.

children.name: text
children: p.

children.name: text
children: Emergency exits and equipment are not to be obstructed.

children.name: text
children: q.

children.name: text
children: Any use of or damage to firefighting equipment is to be reported immediately.

children.name: text
children: r.

children.name: text
children: Prompt medical assistance must be sought for any injury received at work and the injury must be reported as soon as possible.

children.name: text
children: {b:Misconduct:}

children.name: text
children: Any person on site, found to have acted in a dangerous way in contravention to our site rules and procedures shall be liable to be removed from site. This includes:

children.name: text
children: a.

children.name: text
children: Wilfully breaching the safety rules or safety procedures.

children.name: text
children: b.

children.name: text
children: Using alcohol or un-prescribed drugs.

children.name: text
children: c.

children.name: text
children: Removing any equipment guard or protective device.

children.name: text
children: d.

children.name: text
children: Operating any machine, plant, or equipment when untrained or without authority.

children.name: text
children: e.

children.name: text
children: Misusing items provided for first aid.

children.name: text
children: f.

children.name: text
children: Recklessly interfering with or misusing anything provided in the interest of health, safety, or welfare at work.

children.name: text
children: g.

children.name: text
children: Defacing or removing notices, signs, labels, or any other warning device.

children.name: text
children: h.

children.name: text
children: Misusing any chemical, flammable substance, toxic material, etc.

children.name: text
children: i.

children.name: text
children: Smoking in designated "No Smoking" areas or whilst using flammable substances.

children.name: text
children: j.

children.name: text
children: Taking part in horseplay or practical jokes.

children.name: text
children: k.

children.name: text
children: Making false declarations or interfering with evidence following an accident or dangerous occurrence.

children.name: text
children: l.

children.name: text
children: Misusing compressed air, electric or pneumatic equipment.

children.name: text
children: m.

children.name: text
children: Overloading lifting equipment.

children.name: text
children: A copy of the Quinn London Health and Safety Policy and plan is available for your inspection if required and will be available on site if you are successful in being awarded this contract.

children.name: text
children: Any issues regarding Health and Safety on site should be referred to our Site Manager in the first instance then, if necessary, to our Safety Officer.
